correctness.rationale: Reflexivity and transitivity give R_a R_a=R_a, so consecutive repeats can be removed from each word. A subsequence path is a path for any containing word by inserting reflexive steps. Every normalized word contains a minimal normalized word, so satisfying the minimal conjunction is equivalent to satisfying the original under every valuation; retaining a selected endpoint per minimal word proves the upper bound on arbitrary frames. For the lower bound, take the prefix trie of those minimal words. There are no consecutive same-label edges on a branch, so the reflexive transitive closure for a given label adds only loops. A walk to a marked leaf must take the unique forward branch in order with optional stays, and exists exactly when the leaf word is a subsequence of the query word. The minimal antichain therefore forces every originally marked leaf to be retained. This concerns subvaluations of the original marked set, not arbitrary relocations of marks. The empty word produces the singleton antichain and one-world witness. For q>=2 the full reduced depth-d layer has q(q-1)^(d-1) members. Every nonempty shorter reduced word has a continuation to that layer; prefix-incomparable words have disjoint continuation sets. The full layer is a subsequence antichain, so the bound is sharp, while for q=1 the only reduced possibilities are the letter and the comparable empty word. The q=2 plateau and q=3 exponential case follow.
